question: Your support agent's loop code sends one request to Claude, runs the tool that Claude requests, and then replies to the customer. In the logs, a customer who asks about a late refund gets no useful answer: Claude requested get_customer, the code ran it, and the loop ended before Claude could call lookup_order. Which loop control flow should you implement?

options.text: Search each response for phrases such as "your request is resolved" and stop the loop when one of these phrases appears.
options.reason: The guide names parsing natural language signals to determine loop termination as an anti-pattern. The loop should use the stop_reason value instead.

options.text: End the loop as soon as a response contains assistant text, because text means Claude has finished its work for the customer.
options.reason: The guide names checking for assistant text content as a completion indicator as an anti-pattern. A response can contain text and still request a tool.

options.text: Run the loop for exactly five iterations on every request, and use this iteration cap as the main signal that the work is complete.
options.reason: The guide names an arbitrary iteration cap as the primary stopping mechanism as an anti-pattern. The loop should stop on the stop_reason value "end_turn".

options.text: Check stop_reason after each response, execute the requested tools and send their results back while it is "tool_use", and end the loop when it is "end_turn".
options.reason: The guide says the agentic loop continues when stop_reason is "tool_use" and terminates when stop_reason is "end_turn". Tool results go back to Claude so it can reason about the next action.
